title: Bihar GK — Quick Facts and Static GK Compendium

blocks.content: Bihar GK — Quick Facts and Static GK Compendium
Consolidates the highest-frequency, exact-recall static facts about Bihar into a single quick-revision chapter — designed for last-minute review before any Bihar-focused exam.

This final chapter deliberately strips away explanation and context, which earlier chapters have already provided in depth, and presents Bihar's most fundamental facts in the dense, quickly scannable format best suited to the final days before an exam. Read it after, not instead of, the fuller chapters — the goal here is rapid recall reinforcement, not first-time learning.

items: Capital — Patna; State Legislature — Bicameral (Legislative Assembly with 243 members, plus a Legislative Council).
Bordering states/country — Nepal (north, international border), West Bengal (east), Jharkhand (south), Uttar Pradesh (west).
Number of administrative divisions — nine (Patna, Tirhut, Saran, Darbhanga, Kosi, Purnia, Bhagalpur, Munger, Magadh).
Principal river — the Ganga, dividing the state into North Bihar and South Bihar; the Kosi is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.
Jharkhand separated from southern Bihar as a distinct state in November 2000.
Mauryan Empire founded — c. 321 BCE, by Chandragupta Maurya (guided by Chanakya); capital at Pataliputra.
Ashoka's Kalinga War and turn to Buddhism — c. 261 BCE; Lion Capital (Sarnath) later adopted as India's national emblem.
Buddha's enlightenment — at Bodh Gaya; Mahavira's nirvana — at Pawapuri.
Nalanda University founded — c. 5th century CE; declined after Bakhtiyar Khilji's invasion, c. 1193 CE; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2016.
Vikramshila founded by — Pala ruler Dharmapala (late 8th/early 9th century CE).
Bihar and Orissa separated from Bengal Presidency — 1912; Orissa further separated from Bihar — 1936.
Champaran Satyagraha — 1917, Mahatma Gandhi's first Satyagraha campaign within India.
Chhath Puja — dedicated to Surya (Sun God); four-day festival (Nahay Khay, Kharna, Sandhya Arghya, Usha Arghya).
Madhubani (Mithila) Painting — GI-tagged folk art tradition of the Mithila region (Madhubani/Darbhanga).
Sonepur Mela — held at the Ganga-Gandak confluence near Patna; one of Asia's largest cattle fairs.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad — first President of India (1950–1962), longest-serving to date; born in Zeeradei, Siwan district.
Karpoori Thakur — twice Bihar CM, social justice pioneer, Bharat Ratna (2024, posthumous); Jayaprakash Narayan — led the 1974–75 JP Movement, Bharat Ratna (1999, posthumous).
GI-tagged products — Shahi Litchi (Muzaffarpur), Mithila Makhana (Darbhanga/Madhubani), Zardalu Mango and Katarni Rice (Bhagalpur), Magahi Paan (Magadh region).
Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme — launched 2 October 2016 under Saat Nischay; loans up to ₹4 lakh, made effectively interest-free from September 2025.
Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana — ₹25,000 one-time incentive for girls passing Class 12 (Intermediate).
Chief Minister (as of writing) — Samrat Choudhary (since 15 April 2026), 24th CM of Bihar, succeeding Nitish Kumar; Governor — Syed Ata Hasnain.
Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) — the state's primary recruitment examination body, analogous to the UPSC.

cells:
Exam Tip

• This chapter is designed as a final-week revision tool — read through it repeatedly in the days before an exam rather than as a first-pass learning resource, since it assumes the detailed context from earlier chapters is already familiar.

• The current government facts (Chief Minister, Governor) reflect a genuinely recent transition — treat these as a snapshot at time of writing and re-verify against a live source before your actual exam date.

• Cross-reference any fact here against the corresponding detailed chapter if you feel uncertain — this compendium is meant to reinforce, not replace, the fuller explanations earlier in the book.
